headline: High risk: Replit Agent’s broad shell/network/write access can leak or mutate Caveman-managed workspace content if the pair shares files or copied outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Caveman can use MCP and reads/writes project notes and CLAUDE.md, while Replit Agent can read/write Repl workspace files. If Caveman’s outputs are copied into the Replit workspace or shared via MCP-like bridges, attacker-controlled content could steer Replit Agent. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and escalated from low.
conditions: IF Caveman outputs are pasted into Replit workspace files or prompts, Replit Agent may follow injected instructions.
IF an MCP or file bridge is added between the agents, prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Keep agent outputs in separate directories.
Require manual review before copying text between agents.
Strip instructions from imported notes before reuse.
Disable any shared MCP bridge unless provenance is tracked.
requires-engineering: add content provenance labels to transferred files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration and has broad network egress. If they share a workspace or copied files, sensitive content can move from Caveman into Replit Agent’s cloud-backed context and onward to third parties. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Caveman stores secrets or sensitive notes in files later opened by Replit Agent, those contents can be exposed.
IF Replit Agent uploads workspace context to external services, copied Caveman data may leave the original environment.
mitigations: Do not place Caveman notes in the Replit workspace.
Move secrets to a separate vault before sharing files.
Review Replit Agent file access before opening imported artifacts.
Redact sensitive sections from project notes first.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data loss prevention.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Caveman supports multiple instances and uses files, while Replit Agent supports multiple instances, writes the filesystem, and modifies git state in a persistent Repl filesystem. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other. The profiles document overlapping mutable surfaces, so conflict risk is real in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repository or workspace concurrently, file clobbering can occur.
IF git state is shared without locking, commits or branches may diverge or be overwritten.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree.
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files.
Use git branches per agent.
Check diffs before merging outputs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Caveman produces content-writing outputs and Replit Agent is a coding agent that can act on workspace files and deployments. If Replit Agent treats Caveman’s text as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into code or deployment changes. The profiles show a plausible producer-consumer chain, but no direct automation is documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses Caveman-generated notes as source-of-truth without verification, mistakes can propagate.
IF Caveman drafts deployment or code instructions that Replit Agent executes, downstream errors can affect the workspace.
mitigations: Require human verification of Caveman outputs before execution.
Separate draft notes from executable files.
Ask Replit Agent to summarize and validate before acting.
Keep deployment actions behind explicit approval.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between writing and execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Replit Agent handles source code, secrets, and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl with broad network egress. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into the shared workspace, the pair can create a residency/retention mismatch and expose secrets outside the intended boundary. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction, so this is a conservative high-risk inference.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Caveman notes and then opened in Replit Agent, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF Replit Secrets or deployment config contains regulated identifiers, cloud processing may violate local policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Store secrets only in approved vaults.
Review retention settings before syncing files.
Use synthetic data for drafts and tests.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries.
